database: local synthetic copy of JMS staging (seed 7, cap 3000)

cases.question: Show me all active surrogates in Screening and list their current substage.
cases.title: Active surrogates in Screening with current substage
cases.sql:
SELECT g.case_id AS "Case ID", g.case_file_name AS "Surrogate", g.stage AS "Stage", COALESCE(x.substage, 'No substage assigned') AS "Current substage"
FROM gc_case g
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT s.gc_case_id, t.title AS substage,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.gc_case_id ORDER BY s.ordering, s.sub_stage_id) AS rn
  FROM custom_sub_stage s
  JOIN template_sub_stage t ON t.sub_stage_id = s.base_sub_stage_id
  WHERE s.stage = 'screening' AND s.completed IS NULL AND s.gc_case_id IS NOT NULL
) x ON x.gc_case_id = g.case_id AND x.rn = 1
WHERE g.case_type = 'surrogate' AND g.active = 1 AND g.stage = 'screening'
ORDER BY g.case_file_name
assumptions: Surrogates are cases of type 'surrogate' (egg donors and sperm donors are excluded).
Active means the case is flagged active (not archived).
Current substage is the earliest not-yet-completed Screening substage in the case's workflow order.
Surrogates in Screening with no screening substages set up are still listed, shown as 'No substage assigned'.

cases.question: Which IP cases are in matching right now? Include the names and emails for both IPs.
cases.title: IP cases currently in the matching stage, with both IPs' names and emails
cases.sql:
SELECT c.case_id AS "Case ID", c.case_file_name AS "Case Name", c.matching_type AS "Matching Type",
 CONCAT_WS(' ', ip1.first_name, ip1.last_name) AS "IP 1 Name", ip1.email AS "IP 1 Email",
 CONCAT_WS(' ', ip2.first_name, ip2.last_name) AS "IP 2 Name", ip2.email AS "IP 2 Email"
FROM ip_case c
JOIN family f ON f.family_id = c.family_id
JOIN contact ip1 ON ip1.contact_id = f.ip_1_id
LEFT JOIN contact ip2 ON ip2.contact_id = f.ip_2_id
WHERE c.stage = 'matching' AND c.active = 1
ORDER BY c.case_id
assumptions: 'In matching right now' means active cases whose current workflow stage is 'matching'. One inactive case in that stage is excluded.
The two IPs are the first and second contacts on the case's family record.
Many cases have only one IP on file, so the IP 2 name and email are blank for them.
I did not use the matching queue entries (matched, sent, broken and so on) to decide this.

cases.question: Which cases have had their profiles approved in the last 30 days?
cases.title: Cases with profile approved in the last 30 days
cases.sql:
SELECT c.case_id AS "Case ID", c.case_file_name AS "Case name", c.case_type AS "Case type", c.stage AS "Stage",
  CASE c.case_type WHEN 'donor' THEN ct.ed_profile_approved WHEN 'surrogate' THEN ct.gc_profile_approved WHEN 'sperm_donor' THEN ct.sd_profile_approved END AS "Profile approved on"
FROM gc_case c
JOIN contact ct ON ct.contact_id = c.gc_id
WHERE CASE c.case_type WHEN 'donor' THEN ct.ed_profile_approved WHEN 'surrogate' THEN ct.gc_profile_approved WHEN 'sperm_donor' THEN ct.sd_profile_approved END >= DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
ORDER BY 5 DESC
assumptions: 'Profile approved' means the approval date recorded on the person's profile: the egg donor profile for donor cases, the carrier profile for surrogate cases, and the sperm donor profile for sperm donor cases.
'Last 30 days' means the 30 days up to now (since 2026-09-21).
This does not use the matching approvals (matches with status 'APPROVED'), which are a different thing.
I checked the data and found 0 cases in this window, so the empty result is genuine. The most recent profile approval for any case is 2026-08-09, and the check covered all three profile types.

cases.question: List egg donors available for a cycle who haven't donated before.
cases.title: Egg donors available for a cycle with no prior donation
cases.sql:
SELECT g.case_id AS case_number, g.case_file_name AS donor_name, g.stage AS stage, g.donor_status AS donor_availability, CASE WHEN p.past_donor = 0 THEN 'No' ELSE 'Not recorded' END AS donated_before
FROM gc_case g
LEFT JOIN ed_profile p ON p.contact_id = g.gc_id
WHERE g.case_type = 'donor'
  AND g.donor_status = 'available'
  AND g.active = 1
  AND (p.past_donor = 0 OR p.past_donor IS NULL)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM retrieval r WHERE r.ed_case_id = g.case_id)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ed_profile p2 WHERE p2.contact_id = g.gc_id AND p2.past_donor = 1)
GROUP BY g.case_id, g.case_file_name, g.stage, g.donor_status, CASE WHEN p.past_donor = 0 THEN 'No' ELSE 'Not recorded' END
ORDER BY g.case_file_name
assumptions: Egg donors are donor cases whose donor status is 'available' (available for a cycle).
Only active cases are included.
'Haven't donated before' means the profile is not flagged as a past donor and the donor has no recorded egg retrievals.
Most available donors have no past-donor answer on file; they are included and labelled 'Not recorded' rather than excluded. Only donors marked 'No' are confirmed first-time donors.

cases.question: Which contracts are still waiting on a signature?
cases.title: Contracts still waiting on a signature
cases.sql: select h.signature_request_id as 'Signature request', cr.status as 'Signature status', cr.user_type as 'Signer type', concat_ws(' ', u.first_name, u.last_name) as 'Signer name (where a user)', cr.created as 'Request created', datediff(curdate(), cr.created) as 'Days waiting' from contract_rel cr join hellosign h on h.hellosign_id = cr.parent_id left join user u on u.user_id = cr.user_id and cr.user_type = 'user' where cr.status <> 'signed' order by cr.created
assumptions: There is no contract title in the signing data, so each contract is identified by its e-signature request reference.
'Still waiting on a signature' means a signer's request has not reached 'signed': sent, viewed, or undelivered (the last means the notice did not reach them).
Each row is one signer's request; a request with several signers appears once per signer.
Signer names are shown only for regular users; other signer types (admins, non-platform users) show blank.
The status on each signer's request is used, not the overall completion date on the request, which sometimes disagrees.

cases.question: Show me which intended parents have never logged into their portal.
cases.title: Intended parents who have never logged into their portal
cases.sql: SELECT u.user_id AS `User ID`, u.first_name AS `First name`, u.last_name AS `Last name`, u.email AS `Email`, u.created AS `Account created`, CASE WHEN u.active = 1 THEN 'Active' ELSE 'Inactive' END AS `Account status` FROM `user` u WHERE u.user_type = 'IP' AND u.last_login IS NULL ORDER BY u.created
assumptions: Intended parents are portal accounts of type 'IP'; IP representatives are excluded.
'Never logged in' means the account has no recorded last-login date.
Inactive accounts are included and flagged in the status column.
Accounts are listed individually, not grouped by family or case.

cases.question: Which cases have active, incomplete campaigns right now?
cases.title: Cases with active, incomplete campaigns
cases.sql: SELECT COALESCE(g.case_file_name, i.case_file_name) AS "Case", CASE WHEN g.case_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'GC / ED / SD case' WHEN i.case_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'Intended parent case' ELSE 'Unlinked' END AS "Case Kind", COALESCE(g.stage, i.stage) AS "Case Stage", cc.internal_title AS "Campaign", cc.case_type AS "Campaign Case Type", cc.flow_status AS "Flow Status", cc.flow_date AS "Next Step Date", cc.created AS "Enrolled On" FROM case_campaign cc LEFT JOIN gc_case g ON g.case_id = cc.assigned_gc_case LEFT JOIN ip_case i ON i.case_id = cc.assigned_ip_case WHERE cc.active = 1 AND cc.completed IS NULL ORDER BY cc.created DESC
assumptions: 'Active' means the case's campaign enrollment is switched on (this is true for every enrollment).
'Incomplete' means the enrollment has no completion date recorded. Some of these still show a flow status of 'finished', so the status and the completion date don't always agree.
Each row is one campaign enrollment, so a case enrolled in several campaigns appears more than once.
Enrollments are linked to a case through the assigned GC/ED/SD case, or else the assigned intended-parent case. Enrollments with neither link show as 'Unlinked'.
I did not filter on whether the campaign definition itself is enabled.

cases.question: How many open To Dos does each admin currently have assigned to them?
cases.title: Open To Dos currently assigned to each admin
cases.sql:
SELECT CONCAT(a.first_name, ' ', a.last_name) AS admin_name,
  COALESCE(SUM(t.src = 'case'), 0) AS open_case_todos,
  COALESCE(SUM(t.src = 'general'), 0) AS open_general_todos,
  COALESCE(SUM(t.src = 'contact'), 0) AS open_contact_todos,
  COUNT(t.src) AS total_open_todos
FROM admin a
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT 'case' AS src, task_assigned_to_id FROM case_task WHERE completed IS NULL AND task_status <> 'completed'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'general', task_assigned_to_id FROM general_task WHERE completed IS NULL AND task_status <> 'completed'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'contact', task_assigned_to_id FROM contact_task WHERE completed IS NULL AND task_status <> 'completed'
) t ON t.task_assigned_to_id = a.admin_id
GROUP BY a.admin_id, a.first_name, a.last_name
ORDER BY total_open_todos DESC, admin_name
assumptions: 'To Dos' covers all three kinds of admin tasks: case tasks, general tasks and contact tasks. The report shows each kind separately and a total.
A To Do is open if it has no completion date and its status is not 'completed'. The status field alone was unreliable, because some tasks marked 'not started' or 'in progress' have completion dates.
Deferred and pending-input tasks count as open.
All admins are listed, including inactive ones and those with zero open To Dos.
Tasks with no assigned admin are excluded.

cases.question: Which surrogates are still waiting on their profile to be approved?
cases.title: Surrogates still awaiting profile approval
cases.sql:
SELECT g.case_file_name AS "Surrogate", g.stage AS "Case stage", s.status AS "Status", a.admin_id AS "Assigned admin ID", g.created AS "Case created"
FROM gc_case g
JOIN contact c ON c.contact_id = g.gc_id
LEFT JOIN status s ON s.status_id = g.status_id
LEFT JOIN admin a ON a.admin_id = g.assigned_admin
WHERE g.case_type = 'surrogate'
  AND g.active = 1
  AND c.sd_profile_approved IS NULL
ORDER BY g.created
assumptions: Surrogates are cases of type 'surrogate'.
A surrogate is 'waiting on profile approval' if her surrogate profile has no approval date recorded yet.
Only active cases are included; archived or inactive cases are left out.
Assigned admin is shown as an ID only, not a name.

cases.question: Show me egg donor profiles that haven't been approved by the agency yet.
cases.title: Egg donor profiles not yet approved by the agency
cases.sql:
SELECT p.profile_id AS `Profile ID`, c.first_name AS `First name`, c.last_name AS `Last name`, c.email AS `Email`, c.phone_number AS `Phone`, c.created AS `Contact created`, p.user_submitted AS `Submitted by donor (1=yes)`
FROM ed_profile p
JOIN contact c ON c.contact_id = p.contact_id
WHERE c.ed_profile_approved IS NULL
ORDER BY c.created DESC
assumptions: A profile counts as approved by the agency when its donor's contact record has an egg donor profile approval date; profiles with no approval date are treated as not yet approved.
Approval is recorded per person, so if a person has several profiles, all of them show up or are left out together.
All egg donor profiles are included regardless of the donor's status or case progress.

cases.question: Pull a list of sperm donors whose profiles are pending approval.
cases.title: Sperm donors with profiles pending approval
cases.sql:
SELECT g.case_id AS "Case ID", g.case_file_name AS "Sperm Donor", s.status AS "Status", g.stage AS "Stage", g.created AS "Case Created", CASE WHEN g.active = 1 THEN 'Active' ELSE 'Inactive' END AS "Active?", a.first_name AS "Assigned Admin First Name", a.last_name AS "Assigned Admin Last Name"
FROM gc_case g
JOIN status s ON s.status_id = g.status_id
LEFT JOIN admin a ON a.admin_id = g.assigned_admin
WHERE g.case_type = 'sperm_donor' AND s.status LIKE '%Approval%'
ORDER BY g.created DESC
assumptions: Sperm donors are cases whose type is sperm donor.
Pending approval means the donor's current status is 'Pending IP Approval' (the only approval-type status in the system).
'Pending Review' status was not counted as pending approval; one sperm donor has it.
Inactive (archived) cases are included and flagged in the Active column.

cases.question: Show me intended parents whose profile has been approved.
cases.title: Intended parent families with approved profiles
cases.sql:
SELECT f.family_id AS "Family ID",
       CONCAT_WS(' ', c1.first_name, c1.last_name) AS "Intended Parent 1",
       c1.email AS "Parent 1 Email",
       CONCAT_WS(' ', c2.first_name, c2.last_name) AS "Intended Parent 2",
       c2.email AS "Parent 2 Email",
       f.profile_approved AS "Profile Approved On"
FROM family f
JOIN contact c1 ON c1.contact_id = f.ip_1_id
LEFT JOIN contact c2 ON c2.contact_id = f.ip_2_id
WHERE f.profile_approved IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY f.profile_approved DESC
assumptions: An intended parent profile counts as approved when the family has an approval date recorded.
Each row is one intended parent family, showing the first parent and, where there is one, the second parent.
Results are sorted with the most recently approved first.
